evidence.quote: Authenticate to the Lever API via basic auth by providing an API key as the username and leaving the password blank.
A paginated list response will include a next attribute that includes an offset token
we allow a steady state number of 10 requests/second per API key
Lists all audit events in your Lever account, sorted in descending chronological

assumptions: The provided documentation was cut off before the 'List all users' page. The /users path is inferred from the table of contents, the users:read:admin scope and the pagination section, which names users as a paginated list.

User record field names (id, email, name, accessRole, createdAt) are not shown in the source. id, email and name are borrowed from the user object shown in audit events. accessRole and createdAt are unconfirmed guesses and may need checking.

Status, user type and last-active fields are left empty because the source does not document them. The source lists 'Deactivate a user' and 'Reactivate a user' endpoints, but I could not confirm whether deactivated users are returned by default or need an extra parameter.

The API has no per-user last-active field in the source, so usage uses the audit log, counting successful sign-ins (user.authentication:succeeded) as activity. Users who never sign in during the window will look inactive.
Audit events are a paid add-on, so many Lever accounts will not have this endpoint. The plan name 'Audit Events add-on' is my wording.
The audit log has no documented maximum time window, so none is set.
Rate limit is stated as about 10 requests per second, which I converted to 600 per minute. The source says these defaults may vary and gives no rate-limit headers.

API keys are tied to the account and can carry confidential-data access only if granted when the key is created. OAuth is only open to registered partner apps. Both are listed, with the API key first because it is the simplest route.
The default page size of 100 and the 'limit' and 'offset' parameter names come from the pagination section. The 'next' and 'hasNext' response fields come from the list format section.
